text:
support-bot: New ticket forwarded from AcmeApp — reported intermittent SSE disconnects followed by duplicate partial outputs when their client reconnects. Correlation ID: cid-9f3b2e. Payload attached.

Lina P: I reproduced locally with their repro steps. Steps: open SSE, send prompt, after ~18s connection drops, client reconnects with same idempotency token, gets repeated partial continuations (looks like overlapping tokens). They sent a minimal repro gist: https://gist.github.com/acme/repro-sse (shared in ticket).

Tony C: Customer says it started after a recent SDK bump (0.5.2 -> 0.6.0). They rolled that back and issue reduced but still happens sometimes. Asking for timeline and whether billing was affected.

Ingrid S: Can you paste the raw SSE stream (with sequence markers) from their capture? Need to check whether server emitted identical chunks or if client replayed.

Lina P: Paste of captured SSE (sanitized):
```
event: token
data: {"seq": 42, "chunk": "The answer so far..."}

event: token
data: {"seq": 43, "chunk": " and continuing."}

-- socket disconnect (RST) --
(reconnect with header: Idempotency-Key: acme-xyz-123, Resume-After: 43)

event: token
data: {"seq": 44, "chunk": " and continuing."}
```

Ravi K: Two hypotheses: 1) client resends last acked seq (race) and our server treated Resume-After as a hint but re-emitted overlapping tokens because dedup window not keyed by sequence. 2) SDK 0.6.0 changed reconnect timing causing double-send.

Ingrid S: I pulled logs for cid-9f3b2e: server shows last_sent_seq=43, then client reconnect arrives with Idempotency-Key=acme-xyz-123 but no resume_offset header; our runtime currently dedups only full-request hashes for 60s, not stream sequence ranges. Log excerpt:
```
[2025-10-12T14:12:18Z] cid-9f3b2e stream_write seq=42 size=128
[2025-10-12T14:12:19Z] cid-9f3b2e stream_write seq=43 size=64
[2025-10-12T14:12:36Z] cid-9f3b2e conn_reset remote=1.2.3.4
[2025-10-12T14:12:36Z] cid-9f3b2e reconnect idempotency=acme-xyz-123
[2025-10-12T14:12:36Z] cid-9f3b2e stream_write seq=44 size=42
```

Ravi K: That matches — server emitted seq=44 after reconnect. The duplicate partial output likely came from client replaying buffered seq=43 that they didn't ack locally. We should handle two things: a server-side resume protocol (client sends resume_after, server continues from that seq without re-emitting) and stronger dedup keys per-stream seq.

Lina P: Customer wants temporary mitigation. Recommended steps I proposed: 1) Use non-streaming generation (single response) until we patch. 2) Client change: on reconnect, wait 200ms before re-sending previously-received chunks; prefer to request resume_after header with last acked seq. They asked for an example.

Ingrid S: Sample SSE reconnect pattern we can recommend:
```http
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-1
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Idempotency-Key: acme-xyz-123
# on reconnect:
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-1&resume_after=43
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Idempotency-Key: acme-xyz-123
```
Server should not resend seq<=resume_after. We're not honoring resume_after yet.

Tony C: Billing question — Maria, can you check if duplicate tokens inflated their bill for last 24h? Customer reported a spike.

Maria B: Looking. Preliminary: there were ~1200 extra tokens billed for cid-9f3b2e window. It's small, but we should compensate and add protective credits if we caused duplicates. I can issue a refund/credit.

Ravi K: Action items:
- @Ingrid S: add dedup-by-(idempotency_key, seq) logic and ensure server respects resume_after param (hotfix) — target: patch to staging today, roll to prod in next 24-48h.
- @Ravi K: add unit + integration tests to runtime to simulate reconnects and check no duplicate emissions.
- @Lina P: send customer mitigation steps and workaround (non-stream or resume_after) and confirm SDK rollback option.
- @Tony C: coordinate customer comms and credit from Maria.

Ingrid S: I started a branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/fix/sse-resume (WIP). Main issue: our streaming buffer uses a per-connection ring buffer and on reconnect we spawn a new conn and replay writer. Need to persist last_sent_seq in durable metadata keyed by idempotency; will update.

Ravi K: Also note race where two reconnect attempts within 100ms caused duplicate generation because dedupe window used a short TTL. We'll extend dedupe TTL to 5min for idempotency-keys and make per-seq idempotency the source of truth.

Lina P: Customer reply: "Thanks, will try resume_after immediately. SDK team checking rollback." They asked for a concrete timeline for prod fix.

Ingrid S: ETA: staging patch this afternoon, small rollout to 10% canary tomorrow morning, full rollout by EOD tomorrow if no regressions. I'll post PR and link tests.

Tony C: I'll promise a credit and keep them patched. Lina, please paste comms draft here once ready so I can review.

Maria B: I'll prepare a $75 credit and mark as incident-related.

Lina P: Draft comms: "Hi — thanks for the repro. Short term: use resume_after or non-stream mode; we recommend holding off on SDK 0.6.0 until our patch. We're prioritizing a fix and will apply a credit for duplicate tokens this window. ETA for canary: tomorrow morning PST." Thoughts? :thumbsup:

Ravi K: Sounds good. Add link to the SDK rollback instructions and the sample resume_after header.

Ingrid S: PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3456 — tests added. Will update once canary is scheduled.

support-bot: Ticket updated: status=investigating, linked-pr=3456, sla=48h.

Lina P: I'll follow up with the customer after canary is live. Closing thread for day; ping me if anything blocks the rollout. :wave:
